clue.text: Funny mineral found in low part of ridge

indicators.note: the mineral is said to be found inside the ridge word, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks
mica is a flaky silicate mineral

explanation.surface: A geologist finds an amusing rock in a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low part of ridge' reads like scenery, but it is a mountaineer's word for a pass; 'found in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that provokes laughter; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Prestige long held by court

indicators.note: the long word is held inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Fame is a long-standing thing at the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the prestige, but here it is the verb, to yearn; 'held by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means distinction or status that brings respect.

clue.text: Companion of gangster, leader of criminals around America, getting slug?

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
US is America

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of criminals

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend and the head of a crime ring tour the States, getting hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting slug?' looks like a punch, but the slug is the creature; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a shell-less mollusc, so the slug is an example of the class.

clue.text: Ruler artist used after beginning to create sign faultlessly

indicators.note: the artist letters come after everything else
beginning to picks the first letter of create

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
off pat means perfectly, without fault
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist creates a flawless emblem for a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the queen who ruled ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Support reform, securing objective with money

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the reform word holds the objective

parts.note: to alter is to reform or change
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A campaigner backs reform to reach a goal through cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' and 'reform' read as a political slogan; 'securing' is the container signal around the objective.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that must by law be accepted in payment.

clue.text: One telling jokes and, in places, running around

indicators.note: the word 'and' is set inside the reversed places word
running around signals the word for places is turned back to front

parts.note: to place something is to put it, so places gives puts

explanation.surface: A comedian dashes about from venue to venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running around' turns the places word to STUP, and 'in' houses AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up is a comedian who performs solo routines on stage.

clue.text: Features that are odd in skewed picture

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of skewed are the features picked out

explanation.surface: A distorted photograph shows strange things.
explanation.walkthrough: The first, third and fifth letters of SKEWED are S, E, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to see it in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Loft up inside illicit tavern

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
inside says the letters lie within the words illicit tavern

explanation.surface: A secret bar is set up in a roof space.
explanation.walkthrough: The run CITTA sits across 'illiCIT TAvern'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the space under a roof, the same room as an attic.

clue.text: Seducer, forward with endless rubbish, receiving answer after date

indicators.note: the date letter comes before everything else, which follows it

parts.note: on means forward, as in moving on

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the trimmed rubbish word holds the answer letter
endless means the last letter of the rubbish word is removed

parts.note: junk is rubbish

explanation.surface: A forward womaniser talks endless nonsense after a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives JUN; 'receiving' takes in A; 'after' puts the date letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary libertine, a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Work creeps do to get income

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Sneaky people do jobs to earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges the letters of CREEPS DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are the money received from a sale or event.

clue.text: Reminder to admit nothing off legal associate

indicators.note: the reminder word lets the other letters in, so they go inside it

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder, as for an actor
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of legal have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer's partner is prompted to confess nothing improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes LLEAG of the legal letters; 'to admit' places those, after O, within the reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a fellow worker or partner, someone you work alongside.

clue.text: Beat with vitality in piece of music

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vitality, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A lively rhythm features in a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine dance, and also a piece of music written for it.

clue.text: Provide joke on the Internet?

parts.note: E- is the prefix for things done online, as in e-mail
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a gag to share online.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply with what is needed.

clue.text: Hopeless endeavour with revolutionary deeds crushed by despicable sort

indicators.note: the deeds are squeezed inside the despicable sort, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for deeds is read backwards

parts.note: deeds are acts

explanation.surface: A rebel cause is quashed by a villain and fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests rebels but turns the deeds word round to STCA; 'crushed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a venture certain to fail, an undertaking without hope.

clue.text: Living derived from management of business etc

indicators.note: management means handling, so the letters are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone earns a living from running a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management of' rearranges BUSINESS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsistence means the means of staying alive, one's livelihood.

clue.text: Recent bad art is terribly irresponsible

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly treated and so rearranged

explanation.surface: An art critic dismisses modern work as reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges the fourteen letters of RECENT BAD ART IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is disorganised and careless, lacking responsible thought.

clue.text: Completely change course, losing initial ease

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: losing initial means the first letter of the change course word goes

parts.note: to deviate is to change course

explanation.surface: A sailor turns about entirely, giving up the easy life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing initial' leaves EVIATE; 'ease' is the verb, to relieve, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain is to relieve or lessen it.

clue.text: Expected graduate to crack most of puzzle

indicators.note: to crack means to break into, so the graduate goes inside
most of means the final letter of the puzzle word is dropped

parts.note: a problem is a puzzle
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate is expected to solve most of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' leaves PROBLE; 'to crack' breaks it open for the graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something probable is likely, so it is anticipated.

clue.text: Writer with judgement penning end of signed enclosure before nap

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the judgement word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a ruling is a judgement

indicators.note: the enclosure word comes before the nap word
end of picks the final letter of signed

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed area of ground
a kip is a nap or sleep

explanation.surface: An author with good judgement writes his name before a snooze in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives D; 'before' sets the enclosure ahead of the nap; 'penning' wraps all three in the judgement word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was the English author of The Jungle Book and Kim.

clue.text: Current drink

definitions.meaning: a current of air flowing through a room
a single swallow or a measure of drink, as in beer on tap

explanation.definitionFit: A draught is both a flow of cold air indoors and a gulp of liquid, or beer from the cask.

clue.text: Item of lingerie almost secure

parts.note: nigh means near, almost
to tie is to secure

explanation.surface: A lingerie item is almost done up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Draw out souvenir, right out, on appeal

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed below, so the appeal word follows
out means the right letter is taken from the souvenir word

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake or souvenir
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a keepsake out, right on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' leaves ELIC; 'on' sets the appeal word below it, as this is a down clue. IT for sex appeal is an old slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to evoke or bring out a response.

clue.text: Sausage split, broken by rodent with edge of claw

indicators.note: the split word is broken open with the other letters placed inside

parts.note: to burst is to split open
a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: edge of picks the final letter of claw

explanation.surface: A sausage bursts open after a rat's claw scratches it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' gives W; 'broken by' is the container signal on the split word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bratwurst is a German pork sausage.

clue.text: Agreed line maintained by one officer supporting wife

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed below, so the wife letter is on top
the line is held within the one and officer letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer backs his wife, agreeing to keep in line.
explanation.walkthrough: WILCO is radio jargon for 'will comply'. 'maintained by' puts L between I and CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilco is radio shorthand for will comply, signalling assent.

clue.text: Watch, from 6.50, soldier kept

indicators.note: the soldier is kept inside the letters from the number, so one holds the other

parts.note: 6 is VI and 50 is L in Roman numerals
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A guard is posted from ten to seven, with a soldier on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 6.50 looks like a time, but it is Roman numerals; 'kept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of keeping watch, often through the night.

clue.text: Energy shown by second of slips after catch with roll

indicators.note: the energy and slips letters follow the catch word

parts.note: to bag something is to catch it
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: second of picks the second letter of slips

explanation.surface: A cricketer shows energy in the slips after a catch with a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPS is the cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper; its second letter is L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll.

clue.text: Great enthusiast about to imbibe wine after time

indicators.note: imbibe means take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: the wine follows the time letter

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A keen fan is about to drink wine after a long wait, which is great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the time letter before the wine; 'to imbibe' puts both inside the enthusiast and about letters. Asti is an Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is an informal word for excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Astute pilot

explanation.definitionFit: Fly is British slang for sharp-witted, and to fly a plane is to pilot it.

clue.text: Measure of disorder in record about work

indicators.note: the record word goes about the work word, surrounding it

parts.note: an entry is an item recorded in a log or register
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone notes down the chaos in a work log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a disc, but it is a logbook item; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, entropy quantifies how disordered or random a system is.

clue.text: People in Spain allowed to form group

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: the people word is set inside the letters for Spain and allowed

parts.note: to let is to allow
men means people

explanation.surface: Spaniards are permitted to join together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People in Spain' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and Spain is only its vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: An element can mean a section of a larger body, as in the criminal element.
